subproblems.statement: Let ι(v) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons 0 (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ v)) for v ∈ ℝ^m, e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ ℝ^{m+1}, |γ| := covectorEuclideanNorm γ (the Euclidean norm of the coefficients γ(b_{I 0}, …) over strictly increasing coordinate tuples I, b = EuclideanSpace.basisFun) and ‖γ‖ the operator norm of a covector γ. (C1) For all m, k ∈ ℕ, every (k+1)-covector γ on ℝ^{m+1} and every k-covector γ′ on ℝ^m with γ′(v) = γ(Fin.cons e₀ (fun i => ι(v i))) for all v : Fin k → ℝ^m: |γ′| ≤ |γ|. (C2) For all m, q ∈ ℕ, every q-covector γ on ℝ^{m+1} and every q-covector γ′ on ℝ^m with γ′(v) = γ(fun i => ι(v i)) for all v : Fin q → ℝ^m: |γ′| ≤ |γ|. (C3) For all P, n ∈ ℕ and every n-covector α on ℝ^P: |α| ≤ √(P^n)·‖α‖.

Source: step 1 of the parent-supplied proof (coefficient bounds (C1), (C2), (C3)), written out for the exact SimonGMT definition of covectorEuclideanNorm. Conjunct (C3) is also the frozen type of the comparator-accepted declaration fiw_ims_sc_covectorNorm_le_opNorm of another DAG branch (candidate commit c8cb71851ed3018dcc8a0a89a946b8610884f81a); its proof is reproduced in step 5.

Notation. ℝ^p = Eucl p; ι(v) := cons(0, v) = (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons 0 (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ v)); e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ ℝ^{m+1}; ι∘v := (fun i => ι (v i)) and (e₀, ι∘v) := Fin.cons e₀ (fun i => ι (v i)) for tuples v; b^{(p)}_i := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin p) ℝ i (= EuclideanSpace.single i 1); for a q-covector γ on ℝ^p (γ : Covector (Eucl p) q), |γ| := covectorEuclideanNorm γ = (Σ_{I : Fin q → Fin p strictly increasing} γ(b_{I 0}, …, b_{I (q−1)})²)^{1/2} with b_i := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin p) ℝ i, and ‖γ‖ is its operator norm.

1. (Basis vectors.) e₀ = b^{(m+1)}_0, because EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply gives b^{(m+1)}_0 = EuclideanSpace.single 0 1. For j : Fin m, ι(b^{(m)}_j) = b^{(m+1)}_{j.succ}: apply the injective map EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ to both sides (ContinuousLinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply) and compare coordinates by Fin.cases: at coordinate 0 the left side is Fin.cons 0 _ 0 = 0 and the right side is (single j.succ 1) 0 = 0 since j.succ ≠ 0; at coordinate i.succ the left side is (single j 1) i and the right side is (single j.succ 1) i.succ, which agree because Fin.succ is injective.
2. (Sums along an injection.) Let A, B be finite types, g : A → B injective, F : B → ℝ with F ≥ 0 and G : A → ℝ with G(a) ≤ F(g(a)) for all a. Then Σ_a G(a) ≤ Σ_a F(g(a)) (Finset.sum_le_sum) = Σ_{b ∈ g(A)} F(b) (Finset.sum_image, using injectivity) ≤ Σ_b F(b) (Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg, F ≥ 0).
3. ((C1).) Let γ, γ′ be as in (C1). Unfolding covectorEuclideanNorm, |γ′| = √S′ and |γ| = √S with S′ := Σ_{I : Fin k → Fin m} G(I), G(I) := (if I strictly increasing then γ′(b^{(m)} ∘ I)² else 0), and S := Σ_{J : Fin (k+1) → Fin (m+1)} F(J), F(J) := (if J strictly increasing then γ(b^{(m+1)} ∘ J)² else 0) ≥ 0. As √ is monotone (Real.sqrt_le_sqrt) it suffices to show S′ ≤ S, which follows from step 2 with g(I) := Fin.cons 0 (fun i => (I i).succ) once we check:
   (a) g is injective: if g(I) = g(I′), evaluating at i.succ gives (I i).succ = (I′ i).succ, hence I i = I′ i for all i.
   (b) If I is strictly increasing, so is g(I): let a < b in Fin (k+1) and use Fin.cases on a and b. If a = 0 = b this contradicts a < b. If a = 0 and b = j.succ, then g(I)(a) = 0 < (I j).succ = g(I)(b) (Fin.succ_pos). If a = i.succ and b = 0, a < b is impossible (Fin.not_lt_zero). If a = i.succ and b = j.succ, then i < j (Fin.succ_lt_succ_iff), so I i < I j and (I i).succ < (I j).succ.
   (c) G(I) ≤ F(g(I)) for every I: if I is not strictly increasing, G(I) = 0 ≤ F(g(I)). Otherwise both `if`s take their first branch by (b), and by the hypothesis on γ′, γ′(b^{(m)} ∘ I) = γ(Fin.cons e₀ (fun i => ι(b^{(m)}_{I i}))); by Fin.cases and step 1 (index 0: e₀ = b^{(m+1)}_0; index i.succ: ι(b^{(m)}_{I i}) = b^{(m+1)}_{(I i).succ}) this tuple equals b^{(m+1)} ∘ g(I). Hence G(I) = F(g(I)).
   So S′ ≤ S and |γ′| ≤ |γ|.
4. ((C2).) Identical, with A := (Fin q → Fin m), B := (Fin q → Fin (m+1)), g(I) := fun i => (I i).succ (injective because Fin.succ is injective; strictly increasing whenever I is, by Fin.succ_lt_succ_iff), and γ′(b^{(m)} ∘ I) = γ(fun i => ι(b^{(m)}_{I i})) = γ(b^{(m+1)} ∘ g(I)) by the hypothesis and step 1.
5. ((C3).) For every I : Fin n → Fin P, ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm gives |α(b ∘ I)| ≤ ‖α‖·Π_i ‖b_{I i}‖ = ‖α‖, the basis vectors having norm 1 (OrthonormalBasis.norm_eq_one). Hence every summand of the sum defining |α|² is at most ‖α‖² (strictly increasing I: square the bound, pow_le_pow_left₀ with sq_abs; other I: 0 ≤ ‖α‖²), and the sum has #(Fin n → Fin P) = P^n summands, so it is at most P^n·‖α‖² (Finset.sum_le_sum, Finset.card_univ). Therefore |α| ≤ √(P^n·‖α‖²) = √(P^n)·‖α‖ (Real.sqrt_le_sqrt, Real.sqrt_mul, Real.sqrt_sq with ‖α‖ ≥ 0). ∎

The map w ↦ Fin.cons 0 w from (Fin m → ℝ) to (Fin (m+1) → ℝ) is ℝ-linear (check additivity and homogeneity coordinatewise with Fin.cases: coordinate 0 gives 0 = 0 + 0 and 0 = c·0). 1. (Preliminaries.) (i) As in the construction of ι: w ↦ Fin.cons 0 w is ℝ-linear (coordinatewise with Fin.cases), so ι is a continuous linear map ℝ^m →L[ℝ] ℝ^{m+1} with ι(v) = (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons 0 (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ v)) definitionally. (iii) The underlying form of exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ n ω is exteriorDerivative ω = extDeriv ω (definitional; use `show`). (iv) Test forms are C^∞, hence differentiable at every point (ContDiff.differentiable). (v) exteriorDerivative_apply: for ω differentiable at y and u : Fin (n+1) → E, dω(y)(u) = Σ_{i : Fin (n+1)} (−1)^i • fderiv ℝ (fun z => ω z (i.removeNth u)) y (u i).    Fix x, put y := cons(s, x) and define the curve f(τ) := ψ(y + τe₀) − τ·ψ′(y) of q-covectors on ℝ^{m+1}. Source: steps 5 and 6 of the parent-supplied proof (definition of [[0,1]]×X(η) := ∫_0^1 X(φ^η_s) ds, its linearity, the bound M(Z) ≤ M(X), the characterization ProdChar and uniqueness; the support inclusion spt Z ⊆ cyl(spt X)). Siblings used: slice_forms (iwl_cr_ci_slice_testForm), vanish_off_support (isoperimetric_apply_eq_zero_of_disjoint_support), current_criterion (dph_iprod_current_of_bound) and slice_continuity (dph_iprod_slice_continuity, conjunct (D1)).

Notation. ℝ^p = Eucl p; cons(s, x) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ x)) ∈ ℝ^{m+1} for s ∈ ℝ, x ∈ ℝ^m; ι(v) := cons(0, v) = (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons 0 (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ v)); e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ ℝ^{m+1}; ι∘v := (fun i => ι (v i)) and (e₀, ι∘v) := Fin.cons e₀ (fun i => ι (v i)) for tuples v; for a q-covector γ on ℝ^p (γ : Covector (Eucl p) q), |γ| := covectorEuclideanNorm γ = (Σ_{I : Fin q → Fin p strictly increasing} γ(b_{I 0}, …, b_{I (q−1)})²)^{1/2} with b_i := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin p) ℝ i, and ‖γ‖ is its operator norm; D^q(ℝ^p) := TestFormOn univ q, D_q(ℝ^p) := GeometricCurrentOn univ q, M := mass; for a test form ω, ω(x) denotes (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl p) q) x; t(y) := EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y 0, tl(y) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y)) and cyl(A) := {y : t(y) ∈ [0,1], tl(y) ∈ A}; spt := support; a family φ : ℝ → D^k(ℝ^m) is a dt-slice family of η ∈ D^{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) on [0,1] if φ(s)(x)(v) = η(cons(s,x))(e₀, ι∘v) for all s ∈ [0,1], x, v; ProdChar(X, Z) (X ∈ D_k(ℝ^m), Z ∈ D_{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1})) means Z(η) = ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds for every η ∈ D^{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) and every dt-slice family φ of η on [0,1].

Let m, k and X ∈ D_k(ℝ^m) with M(X) < ∞; B := M(X).toReal ≥ 0.
1. (Chosen slice families.) For every η ∈ D^{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}), slice_forms (with P := m, m := k) provides φ^η : ℝ → D^k(ℝ^m) with φ^η(s)(x)(v) = η(cons(s,x))(e₀, ι∘v) for all s, x, v. Fix such a choice for every η (the `choose` tactic). In particular φ^η is a dt-slice family of η on [0,1].
2. (Independence of the slice family.) If φ is any dt-slice family of η on [0,1], then φ(s) = φ^η(s) for every s ∈ [0,1] (Subtype.ext, funext x, ContinuousAlternatingMap.ext v: both sides equal η(cons(s,x))(e₀, ι∘v)). Hence ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds = ∫_0^1 X(φ^η(s)) ds by intervalIntegral.integral_congr (uIcc 0 1 = Icc 0 1, Set.uIcc_of_le).
3. (Integrability.) By (D1) of slice_continuity, s ↦ X(φ^η(s)) is continuous on [0,1], hence interval integrable on [0,1] (ContinuousOn.intervalIntegrable_of_Icc).
4. (Linearity.) Put Z₀(η) := ∫_0^1 X(φ^η(s)) ds. For η, η′ ∈ D^{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) the family s ↦ φ^η(s) + φ^{η′}(s) is a dt-slice family of η + η′ (evaluation of forms and covectors is pointwise additive: Pi.add_apply, ContinuousAlternatingMap.add_apply). By step 2, linearity of X (map_add) and intervalIntegral.integral_add (with step 3), Z₀(η + η′) = ∫_0^1 (X(φ^η(s)) + X(φ^{η′}(s))) ds = Z₀(η) + Z₀(η′). For a ∈ ℝ, s ↦ a·φ^η(s) is a dt-slice family of a·η (Pi.smul_apply, ContinuousAlternatingMap.smul_apply), so Z₀(a·η) = ∫_0^1 a·X(φ^η(s)) ds = a·Z₀(η) (map_smul, intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul). Thus Z₀ : D^{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ.
5. (Bound.) If C ∈ ℝ and |η(y)| ≤ C for all y, then (D1) gives |X(φ^η(s))| ≤ B·C for s ∈ [0,1], in particular for s ∈ uIoc 0 1 = Ioc 0 1; intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const gives |Z₀(η)| ≤ B·C·|1 − 0| = B·C.
6. (The current; conjunct (c).) By current_criterion (with P := m+1, q := k+1, U := univ, T₀ := Z₀ and B), there is Z ∈ D_{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) with Z(η) = Z₀(η) for all η and M(Z) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B = M(X) (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal, M(X) ≠ ∞).
7. (Conjunct (a), ProdChar(X, Z).) If φ is a dt-slice family of η on [0,1], then Z(η) = Z₀(η) = ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds by step 2.
8. (Conjunct (b), uniqueness.) Let Z′ satisfy ProdChar(X, Z′). For every η, applying it to the dt-slice family φ^η gives Z′(η) = ∫_0^1 X(φ^η(s)) ds = Z₀(η) = Z(η); hence Z′ = Z (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).
9. (Conjunct (d), support.) spt X = univ ∖ zeroRegion(X) = zeroRegion(X)ᶜ is closed (GeometricCurrentOn.isOpen_zeroRegion), so cyl(spt X) = t⁻¹([0,1]) ∩ tl⁻¹(spt X) is closed (t and tl are continuous). Let y₀ ∈ spt Z and suppose y₀ ∉ cyl(spt X). Choose ρ > 0 with ball(y₀, ρ) ∩ cyl(spt X) = ∅ (Metric.isOpen_iff for the open complement) and put W := ball(y₀, ρ).
   (i) Z vanishes on W. Let η ∈ D^{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) with tsupport η ⊆ W, and let s ∈ [0,1], j_s(x) := cons(s,x). If j_s(x) ∉ tsupport η then η(j_s(x)) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport), so φ^η(s)(x) = 0; thus support φ^η(s) ⊆ j_s⁻¹(tsupport η), which is closed (j_s continuous), and tsupport φ^η(s) ⊆ j_s⁻¹(tsupport η) (closure_minimal). If x ∈ tsupport φ^η(s) ∩ spt X, then j_s(x) ∈ tsupport η ⊆ W, while t(j_s(x)) = s ∈ [0,1] and tl(j_s(x)) = x ∈ spt X (ContinuousLinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply, Fin.cons_zero, Fin.tail_cons, ContinuousLinearEquiv.symm_apply_apply), so j_s(x) ∈ W ∩ cyl(spt X) = ∅, a contradiction. Hence tsupport φ^η(s) and spt X are disjoint and X(φ^η(s)) = 0 by vanish_off_support. By intervalIntegral.integral_congr, Z(η) = ∫_0^1 X(φ^η(s)) ds = ∫_0^1 0 ds = 0.
   (ii) W is open, closure W ⊆ closedBall(y₀, ρ) (closure_ball_subset_closedBall) is compact (isCompact_closedBall, IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset) and closure W ⊆ univ; with (i), W belongs to the family whose union is zeroRegion(Z), so y₀ ∈ W ⊆ zeroRegion(Z) (Set.mem_sUnion, Metric.mem_ball_self), contradicting y₀ ∈ spt Z = univ ∖ zeroRegion(Z). Hence spt Z ⊆ cyl(spt X).
Steps 6–9 give the four conjuncts for this Z. ∎

0. (Identification of boundary slices.) 2. (Conjunct (III).) Admissible ψ satisfy |ψ(y)| ≤ 1 for all y; ψ is continuous with compact support.
4. (Case k = 0.) For admissible ψ, horizontal_slices gives Ψ, Ψ′, and (II) (step 1) with ψ₀ := Ψ(0), ψ₁ := Ψ(1) gives ∂Z(ψ) = X(Ψ(1)) − X(Ψ(0)). By (D2) of slice_continuity (ω := ψ, C := 1), |X(Ψ(s))| ≤ B for every s. Hence ∂Z(ψ) ≤ 2B; take A := 2B.
5. (Case k = j + 1.) The hypothesis with this j and Y := X (k = j + 1 by rfl, HEq.rfl) gives M(∂X) < ∞; let B′ := M(∂X).toReal. For admissible ψ ∈ D^{j+1}(ℝ^{m+1}), horizontal_slices gives Ψ, Ψ′ and slice_forms (P := m, m := j, η := ψ) gives φ with φ(s)(x)(v) = ψ(cons(s,x))(e₀, ι∘v) for all s (in particular a dt-slice family of ψ on [0,1]). Hence ∂Z(ψ) ≤ 2B + B′; take A := 2B + B′. ∎
